what_happened: The scope guard paused the owner decision-briefs line after its last attempt was rejected. That attempt met 8 of 9 criteria. The rejection came from two small gaps: a test fixture where both proposals share one source, and a Pages workflow that checks out only main. The person running Athena lifted the pause by hand. They judged the remaining work small and named, about a 5-minute writer run costing around $2.50 in all, and the owner had asked for these briefs.
cause: The scope guard pauses a line on rejected spend without measuring how close the attempt came. It does not count criteria met, check how small and named the gap is, or compare the retry cost with the spend already made. A near-complete attempt (8 of 9 criteria, two narrow gaps) looks the same as work that has gone off course. Only the person running Athena can lift the pause, so they must work out the retry cost and scope by hand. The pause also does not separate a rejection on a few named, fixable gaps from a rejection that shows the work is off track. The earlier case had the same shape: the guard read a rejection as lost progress when the work was nearly done.
prevention: When the guard is about to pause a line, it should first read the latest verdict. If most criteria are met (for example 8 of 9) and every gap is a named, bounded finding, the guard should not pause. It should queue a targeted retry limited to the named gaps and show the expected cost and mode (a writer run, not a rebuild). It should pause only when the unmet share is large, the gaps are unnamed, or repeated attempts have not narrowed the gap. In that case it should show the verdict summary and the retry estimate, so lifting the pause is an informed one-step decision rather than manual research.
proposed_request: Change the scope guard so it does not pause a line when the latest rejected attempt met most of its acceptance criteria and every remaining gap is a named blocker or major finding. In that case it should queue a targeted retry that addresses only those findings and record the criteria met, the named gaps and the expected retry cost. Keep the pause when the unmet share is large, a finding is unnamed, or two attempts in a row have not reduced the gap. When it does pause, print the criteria met, the named gaps and the estimated retry cost and mode, so the person running Athena can lift it with one command. Acceptance: (1) a test with a verdict of 8 of 9 criteria met and two named findings produces a targeted retry and no pause; (2) a test with 3 of 9 met, or an unnamed finding, still pauses and prints the summary and estimate; (3) a test with two consecutive attempts that do not narrow the gap still pauses; (4) the existing environment-stop and system-caused-rejection behavior is unchanged.
